messages:
katie_cs: FYI — Acme reported a month-end mismatch, dashboard shows 1,204,812 tokens for Mar but invoice lists 1,048,200 tokens and the line items moved ~160k tokens into the STANDARD tier. Customer says no plan change. Can we triage? :eyes:

mike_billing: thx. please paste account id + invoice id and the invoice generation ts so we can correlate. also any screenshots or CSVs from the dashboard helps.

katie_cs: acct: ACME-99321, invoice: INV-2026-03-ACME-22, invoice_ts: 1865432100. attaching dashboard export link: https://redwood-internal.s3/exports/ACME-99321/mar-usage.csv (CSV has per-route token counts).

ana_prod: quick note — I see a subscription consolidation event for that account on 2026-03-28 at 23:55 UTC where we merged a legacy promo seat into the main subscription (internal event id SUB-MERGE-778). Could be attribution change during merge window.

ana_prod: also checked the subscription timeline: customer had PRO plan until 2026-03-28T23:55Z, then consolidated under STANDARD after merge. The effective timestamp looks correct but we have a few downstream jobs that reclassify usage when consolidation events apply retroactively.

katie_cs: here's the dashboard vs billing quick diff I ran locally:
```
-- dashboard total tokens (sum route_tokens) = 1,204,812
-- invoice tokens total (billing_line_items) = 1,048,200
-- delta = 156,612 tokens attributed to STANDARD on invoice but PRO on dashboard
```

tarun_eng: thanks. can you run this repro query in staging billing DB? it recreates attribution across subscription changes:
```sql
SELECT u.event_ts::date AS day, s.plan_before, s.plan_after, SUM(u.tokens) as tokens
FROM usage_events u
LEFT JOIN subscription_events s ON u.account_id = s.account_id
  AND u.event_ts BETWEEN s.effective_ts AND s.next_effective_ts
WHERE u.account_id = 'ACME-99321' AND date_trunc('month', u.event_ts) = '2026-03-01'
GROUP BY 1,2,3
ORDER BY day;
```

tarun_eng: main thing to check is how we populate s.next_effective_ts for merge events — if it's NULL we may be backfilling differently for invoice job vs dashboard job.

katie_cs: ran that query (attached result CSV) — output shows 1,048,200 tokens under STANDARD (post-merge) starting 2026-03-28 and 156,612 tokens under PRO before that. Dashboard export still shows those 156k under PRO though.

billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-03-ACME-22 generated by pipeline v2.3.1 at 1865432100, policy: consolidate_and_rollup = true.

mike_billing: OK looks like invoice pipeline applied the consolidation retroactively (reassigned earlier usage to STANDARD) while dashboard is showing live per-route attribution (pre-merge plan labels). can we confirm which behavior customer expects? definitely a surprise. :grimacing:

katie_cs: customer expects invoice to match dashboard totals. they flagged this as an accounting discrepancy. requested an itemized reconciliation and whether we can apply a credit for the reclassified tokens this month.

tarun_eng: next steps I'll open a billing trace (TRACE-778-A) and check the rollforward/backfill code path — likely an off-by-one in how we set next_effective_ts for merge events. if that's the case, option A: regenerate invoice with original attribution, option B: provide credit and update dashboard to show consolidated view with note.

katie_cs: sounds good. please add estimated ETA for root cause and whether a retro invoice regen is safe for production (customer is in enterprise support tier).

tarun_eng: will update here after TRACE completes. prelim ETA 24h for root cause + 48h for regen plan if safe. tagging @mike_billing for regen approval. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
